newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria police step up fight against car theft.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria police step up fight against car theft.

text.p: Bulgaria's police said on Tuesday they planned to crack down on the trade in stolen luxury cars by helping buyers to check the engine numbers of vehicles offered for sale.

Organised groups, often working with gangs in Western Europe, alter the appearance of stolen cars, change licence plates, scrape off engine and car body numbers and engrave new ones to match forged documents.

"Working groups at the (Interior) Ministry are preparing a procedure under which scraped off engine and car body numbers would be revealed by a special apparatus and each conscientious buyer would be interested in such checks," national police director Slavcho Bosilkov told reporters.
He said there would be a fee for the service.
Car thefts make up one fifth of all crime in Bulgaria and police say many stolen cars pass through the Balkan country to Ukraine and Russia and even to the Far East.

Bosilkov said police were currently looking for 51,400 stolen cars, all luxury marques such as Mercedes, BMW, Audi and Porsche. "Some of them are re-exported and some of them stay in the country," he told Reuters.
Bosilkov said that for the first five months of the year the number of stolen cars had decreased to 4,639 from 5,170 during the same period last year.
"This tendency has continued in the last two months as we have 323 stolen cars less than the 1850 vehicles stolen during the same period last year," he added.
Bulgaria is planning to tighten its laws in line with European Union legal codes aimed at cracking down on organised crime.
Officials said amendments to the criminal code and several other laws were almost ready to be proposed to the government and then to parliament for approval.
Bulgaria's new government, which took office on May 21, vowed to combat organised crime and corruption.
